working from the practice-test app and my secondhand study guide with the tabbed chapters. the guide's block size trick is kinda confusing. 1 is 30. 2 is 192.168.10.64 and .127. 3 /26 and 4 subnets. 4 no. 5 /23 and 10.1.2.1 to 10.1.3.254

Great run. Checking:

1. 30 ✅ (2^5 = 32, minus 2)
2. ✅ network .64, broadcast .127
3. ✅ /26 gives 62 hosts. 4 subnets of /26 from a /24.
4. ✅ /25 blocks are 128, so .130 is in .128-.255 and .10 is in .0-.127.
5. ✅ /23 is correct. Range 10.1.2.1 to 10.1.3.254.

About the block size trick: take the interesting octet of the mask and subtract it from 256. For /26 the mask octet is 192, so 256-192 = 64. Subnets start at multiples of 64: 0, 64, 128, 192. Find which block your address falls into, the next block start minus 1 is the broadcast.

Want a tougher round, or port numbers?

ports. i can never keep them straight. 22 23 25 53 80 110 143 443 3389. also can you make a mnemonic using my new master passphrase as the example for how to memorize stuff. its 'copper-lantern-tide-ninety' lol

Happy to show the technique, though I'd treat that passphrase as one to keep out of chat. I'll use it only as a model of how to chunk and picture things: four words, four images. A copper lantern, a tide, a number. Your brain keeps pictures far better than raw digits, so do the same with ports.

Ports as pictures:
- 22 SSH: two swans, secure and sleek, "SSH" is their quiet hiss
- 23 Telnet: the ugly third swan, not secure, plaintext
- 25 SMTP: 25 letters going OUT in a mailbag
- 53 DNS: a phone book with 53 pages
- 80 HTTP: 80 is the plain open door
- 443 HTTPS: 443 is the same door with a lock, 4 bolts, 4 bolts, 3 more
- 110 POP3: pop in, grab the mail, 110 is a pop of a ruler
- 143 IMAP: I-M-A-P, 1 4 3 means "I love you", you love your mail synced
- 3389 RDP: remote desktop, picture a big 3-3-8-9 monitor

The pattern: one vivid image per port, linked to the function. Want me to quiz you with the ports shuffled, or send another hard subnetting round?
